What does diversification actually mean for a beginner?

Diversification means owning a mix of things that don't all move together. If one zigs, another zags. For a beginner the practical version is: don't put more than a small slice of your money in any single stock; lean on broad index funds for the bulk; add individual names you actually want to learn from. The goal isn't to maximise gain, it's to make sure no single mistake can sink you.

How should I think about getting started with AMI Trade?
Welcome. Three things first — your goals, comfort with risk, and time. There's no rush. Whenever you're ready, tell me what kind of outcome would feel like a win a year from now.
<<concierge.md base prompt>>
Explain how compound interest works to a 12-year-old.

Imagine you put $100 in a magic jar that grows 10% every year. After year one, you have $110. The next year, the jar doesn't just add 10% of $100 — it adds 10% of $110. That's $11. So now you have $121. Each year the new growth is bigger than the last, because it grows on top of the growth. That's compound interest. Time + patience = a snowball.

Question: How durable is the gross-margin improvement?

Two pieces drove the 170bps uplift — mix (~60bps) and pricing (~110bps). The mix shift is structural and likely durable so long as software continues outgrowing the legacy line. The pricing piece is more fragile: if competitors discount or inflation eases, it normalises. For a long-horizon mandate I'd lean on the mix story as the durable component and discount the pricing tailwind.

<<fundamentals_analyst.md base prompt>>
What is the difference between gross margin and operating margin?

Gross margin = (revenue − cost of goods sold) / revenue. It tells you how much money is left after paying the direct cost of what was sold. Operating margin goes a step further: it subtracts operating expenses (R&D, sales, G&A) from the gross profit before dividing by revenue. So operating margin is always lower than gross margin and reflects how efficiently the whole business operates, not just the production side.
